headline: North-West SLA failures from a warehouse breakdown are driving enterprise account losses.
body: All the account decline is concentrated in North-West, where fulfilment SLA dropped sharply [E1]. A conveyor failure and picker shortage at WH-07 degraded throughput and produced the SLA misses [E6]. Two named enterprise accounts, Meridian Retail Group and Kalinga Mart, cite missed deliveries as their reason for evaluating a competitor [E3]. No contradicting driver was found, and the SLA-to-churn link is strongly corroborated across accounts.

actions.driver: SLA breaches from WH-07 mechanical failure
actions.action: Offer Meridian and Kalinga a written 3-day SLA commitment
actions.expected_impact: Retain at-risk enterprise accounts before churn finalizes
actions.monitoring: Track SLA % and account status weekly for both accounts

actions.action: Approve onboarding credits for at-risk North-West accounts
actions.expected_impact: Improve odds of reversing migration decisions
actions.monitoring: Monitor renewal/QBR outcomes over next 60 days

what_could_change: Confirmation that WH-07 conveyor and staffing are fixed, and SLA recovers, would validate the fix; a third account citing SLA misses would strengthen the case further.
caveats: Impact is drawn from only two named accounts and one region, so scale beyond North-West is unconfirmed.
